decisions.reason: Connects the session/tool worker to the host installation npm replaces, explains the host dies between remove and linkStuff so the result path is destroyed, treats it as a structural hazard, and preserves the unknown tool outcome instead of calling it a network failure.
Explains content present but dsh/dsh.cmd missing and dsh.ps1 stale pointing at the old tree — the interrupted-install signature — and rejects hand-swapped directories or handmade shims as repair.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: pinned npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1 from outside the dead host regenerating shims, version verified, source checkout aligned to the tag; separates the recorded repair from proposed runtime verification.

Requires recognizing the session runs on the upgrade target and handing off: fully stop the host, pinned external install, restart, hard refresh, verify; distinguishes existing stop/pin rules from the new refuse-inside-the-target discipline and the no-result-means-unknown semantics.

Describes a host-self detection preflight comparing the install target with the running host tree plus a command-class guard; uses the version-only alpha.5→rc.1 diff to rule out plugin migration; checks shims, version markers, ghost hosts and plugin loading, with backup cleanup only after confirmation.

caps.reason: Final protocol refuses any in-session or while-live execution and hands the user an external procedure after a full host stop.
Manual directory swaps and hand-written shims are explicitly rejected in favor of the formal external pinned reinstall.
